solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Place like Massachusets could be gas

parts.note: PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street addresses
as means like, in the sense 'such as'
MA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Massachusetts (misspelt in the clue)

explanation.surface: A spot resembling a New England state might turn out to be gaseous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' is a link: the substance is an ionised gas, so the hedge makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: This state of matter is an ionised form of gas, found in stars and neon signs.

clue.text: It could be filthy, it could be cruel

indicators.note: the letters of cruel could be rearranged into another word, so this signals an anagram

explanation.surface: A riddle: something that might be dirty might also be unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the stock phrase 'filthy ___', a contemptuous name for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Money gained dishonestly is proverbially described as filthy, so this word is what could be filthy.

clue.text: Dizzy agent blocking similar soubriquet

indicators.note: one thing blocking another sits in the middle of it, so the jumbled letters go inside

parts.note: similar means the same

indicators.note: dizzy suggests the letters of agent are spinning about into a new order

explanation.surface: A light-headed representative gets in the way of a matching nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dizzy' reads as a description of the agent, but it is the anagram signal; 'blocking' signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A soubriquet is an assumed name, and performers often adopt a professional one for the theatre.

clue.text: Lead on aluminium bait that's artificial

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
a lure is an artificial bait used by anglers

explanation.surface: An angler's tip: put a lead weight on a metal fake bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead on' reads as metal-on-metal, but it is the verb meaning to entice.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to tempt or entice them, which is exactly what this verb means.

clue.text: Completely with one featuring in Carry On Muse

indicators.note: a thing featuring in another appears within it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: to cope is to carry on, manage despite difficulty
all means completely, as in 'all alone'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Sounds like a review: a classical goddess wholly cast in a Carry On film.
explanation.walkthrough: Carry On films are a long-running series of bawdy British comedies; here the words just mean cope.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Muse of epic poetry, one of the nine Greek goddesses of the arts.

clue.text: Do coax from date this disobedience

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them, to con them
to coax is to tempt or entice
of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'
to date someone is to court them

explanation.surface: An instruction to wheedle someone out of an appointment, which is called a kind of defiance.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like an anagram instruction, but each word is a synonym, joined in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to obey a judge's order, or disrupting proceedings, is this offence: disobedience towards a tribunal.

clue.text: Busily sit with Cyril being poet?

indicators.note: busily suggests letters bustling about, so sit and Cyril are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Cyril and a friend sit together working hard, perhaps writing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a song-writer is only loosely a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of song words is a kind of poet, hence the hedging question mark.

clue.text: Suffer rotter batting first

indicators.note: first places the batting piece ahead of the rotter in the answer

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in
a cur is a contemptible man, a rotter

explanation.surface: A scoundrel opens the innings and has a bad time of it.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side currently batting is said to be 'in'; 'first' fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a loss or penalty upon oneself is to suffer it, as in incurring a fine.

clue.text: E.g. earth bank cut back forming feature of city park

parts.note: Earth is an example of a planet

indicators.note: cut back means the word loses its last letter, its back end

parts.note: a reef is a ridge or bank of rock or sand just below the water

explanation.surface: Trimming an earth bank to create a landscaping feature in an urban park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut back' drops the F from REEF. The tree is a hybrid famously lining London squares and parks.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall hybrid with flaking bark tolerates pollution, so it is a familiar sight in urban green spaces.

clue.text: Old at sea recline around an ___ ___

definitions.text: Old at sea recline around an ___ ___

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters are placed on either side of the small word an
at sea means confused, so the letters of recline are jumbled

explanation.surface: Elderly passengers lounge about on a cruise ship, the blank inviting you to name it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'at sea' is the anagram signal and 'around' the insertion, while the blanks stand for the vessel itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger ship is where the old might lounge at sea, so the whole clue paints the vessel.

clue.text: Crack geezer

definitions.meaning: a small split in the skin, caused by cold or wind
British slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A brilliant bloke, or a crack at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a split in the skin from cold and, informally, a man or fellow.

clue.text: Train on vehicle which won't bring you back

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters

parts.words: vehicle which won't bring you back
parts.note: a hearse carries the dead on a one-way trip

explanation.surface: Travel advice: take a train on a vehicle that gives no return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like transport, matching the surface, but it is the verb to practise.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise a performance before giving it is to train for it, the verb sense of train.

clue.text: Reprimand French and complain upfront

indicators.note: upfront puts the complaining word at the front, ahead of the French

parts.note: to carp is to complain or find fault
et is French for and

explanation.surface: Telling off the French and grumbling openly about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upfront' puts CARP ahead of ET, the French for 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul someone over the coals, summoning them for a dressing-down, is the verb to reprimand.

clue.text: Parasite initially found close to meadow

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of found is taken

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.surface: A bloodsucker discovered near the grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: This small jumping insect feeds on the blood of animals, a classic external parasite.

clue.text: Prospect in new places, collecting too

indicators.note: the jumbled letters gather in the other piece, so it goes inside them
new means the letters of places are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: and means too, also

explanation.surface: A view over new sites, which also collect things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospect' suggests a chance or hope, but here it is a scenic view; 'new' is the anagram signal and 'collecting' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is an extensive view of scenery, the sense of 'a fine prospect over the hills'.

clue.text: Document is left after change

indicators.note: after puts the left-hand word following the other in the answer

parts.note: to pass can mean to change from one state to another
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A paper is left behind after a change of trains.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the nautical term for the left side of a ship; 'after' sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: This official travel paper confirms identity and nationality, a document carried across borders.

clue.text: Make a quick buck for, well, alway

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
fit means well, healthy
alway is an archaic word for always, and e'er is the poetic form of ever, always

explanation.surface: Someone forever out for a fast profit, healthy or not.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit a shortage by charging excessive prices is to cash in quickly, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Rare slip upset quid pro quo

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of rare slip are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: An unusual blunder overturned triggers a tit-for-tat response.
explanation.definitionFit: A retaliation in kind, giving back what one received, is a quid pro quo of a hostile sort.

clue.text: Nurse, single, getting over chap from La-La Land?

parts.note: nurses are traditionally called angels for their care

indicators.note: getting over means the word flips over, read backwards

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: A nurse, unattached, gets over a fellow from a dreamy fantasy world.
explanation.walkthrough: La-La Land is a nickname for Los Angeles; 'getting over' reverses ONE to ENO.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or resident of Los Angeles, nicknamed La-La Land, is called by this demonym.

clue.text: Ordinary writer is generally accessible

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for Ordinary, as in the old O-level exam
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An everyday author is usually easy to approach.
explanation.walkthrough: O for Ordinary comes from the former British O-level exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available to everyone, with no restriction on entry, is public and freely accessible.

clue.text: From Uppsala, a mighty welcome

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words Uppsala, a mighty

explanation.surface: A hearty greeting from the Swedish city of Uppsala.
explanation.definitionFit: This Arabic-derived greeting, often with a low bow, is a respectful salutation or welcome.

clue.text: Moneylender's safe in old city

indicators.note: in means the safe word is placed inside the old city

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
sure means safe, certain

explanation.surface: A lender's money is secure in an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moneylender's' is the definition plus 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who lends money, especially at exorbitant interest, is a usurious financier.

clue.text: Drive back social outcast that must be put up

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is raised so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a leper is a person shunned by society

explanation.surface: Repel an outcast who has to be given lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: To force an attacker to retreat is to drive them back, ward off.

clue.text: Cool Bordeaux bottles? One is blown

indicators.note: one word bottles another by holding it inside

parts.note: claret is red wine from Bordeaux
in means cool, fashionable

explanation.surface: Chilled wine in bottles, and a woodwind to play at the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like a noun, a plural of bottle, but it is the verb meaning holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument is played by blowing through a reed mouthpiece, so it is something blown.

clue.text: Shifting Earl to the north, Napoleon gains key wood

indicators.note: shifting means a letter is taken from its place and put elsewhere in the word
in a down clue north is the top, so the letter goes to the front

parts.note: Boney was the British nickname for Napoleon Bonaparte

explanation.surface: An earl is moved north while Napoleon picks up an important forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gains' is a link. The black keys of a piano were traditionally made of this wood.
explanation.definitionFit: This dense black timber was used for the black keys on pianos, so it is wood for keys.

clue.text: Caught by a Red Cap in ____?

definitions.text: Caught by a Red Cap in ____?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Redcap is British slang for a military policeman, an MP

explanation.surface: Arrested by a military policeman in an army base.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcaps are British military police, named after their red caps; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A military base where soldiers are quartered is where a soldier would be arrested by army police.

clue.text: Badger-hunter knowing trail around Australia

indicators.note: around means the knowing word goes round the abbreviation for Australia

parts.note: sage means wise, knowing
to dog someone is to trail or follow them

explanation.surface: A wise hunter follows badgers' tracks across Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The dachshund, nicknamed for its long body, was bred in Germany to hunt badgers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dachshund is German for badger hound, as the breed was developed to chase badgers into setts.

clue.text: Dwelling on upland pasture is bombed

indicators.note: on means the dwelling sits after the pasture, placed upon it

parts.note: a fell is a stretch of high moorland pasture in northern England
a flat is a dwelling, an apartment

explanation.surface: A home on high moorland has been hit by bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: A fell is upland moor in northern England. 'is' is a link; 'bombed' means failed.
explanation.definitionFit: A show that bombed failed completely, the idiom for a joke or performance that gets no response.

clue.text: Title about bohemian believer to the end

indicators.note: about means the title wraps round the bohemian word

parts.note: Mr is a title for a man
arty means bohemian, unconventionally artistic

explanation.surface: A titled man round arty circles keeps the faith to the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dies for their faith rather than renounce it held their belief until death.
